pr_title: kernel: sched: Disable FPU context when thread ends
pr_body:
The following is with respect to ARM64, although this issue likely exists on other architectures too.

When `CONFIG_FPU_SHARING` is enabled each `k_thread` struct has a saved floating point context (`saved_fp_context`).
During a context switch, the current FPU owner's (`_current_cpu->arch.fpu_owner`) registers are saved to its `saved_fp_context`, and the destination threads FPU registers are loaded from its `saved_fp_context`.

When a thread ends, it does not release ownership of the FPU (`_current_cpu->arch.fpu_owner`).
This is problematic if the `k_thread` struct was allocated on the stack.
The next context switch will save the FPU registers into `k_thread -> saved_fp_context` which may now be out of scope.
This will likely (but not always) result in a crash.

Adding `arch_float_disable(thread);` when a thread ends disables preservation of floating point context information, fixing this issue

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61454
Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/60678
pr_comments: Never mind my other (since deleted) comment, the FPU registers are saved/restored lazily by trapping FPU access exceptions. After adding some actual floating point operations I could see the FPU owner getting updated correctly

issue_context.title: ARM64: Saved FPU context accessed after thread ends
issue_context.body:
The following is with respect to ARM64, although this issue likely exists on other architectures too.

When `CONFIG_FPU_SHARING` is enabled each `k_thread` struct has a saved floating point context (`saved_fp_context`).
During a context switch, the current FPU owner's (`_current_cpu->arch.fpu_owner`) registers are saved to its `saved_fp_context`, and the destination threads FPU registers are loaded from its `saved_fp_context`.

When a thread ends, it does not release ownership of the FPU (`_current_cpu->arch.fpu_owner`).
This is problematic if the `k_thread` struct was allocated on the stack.
The next context switch will save the FPU registers into `k_thread -> saved_fp_context` which may now be out of scope.
This will likely (but not always) result in a crash.

**To Reproduce**

Source:

	#include <zephyr/kernel.h>
	
	static K_THREAD_STACK_DEFINE(thread_stack, 4096);
	
	static void thread_func(void *arg1, void *arg2, void *arg3)
	{
		printk("");
	}
	
	static void run_thread(void)
	{
		struct k_thread thread; // <-- make static to prevent crash
		k_thread_create(&thread, thread_stack, K_THREAD_STACK_SIZEOF(thread_stack),
				thread_func, NULL, NULL, NULL, 0, 0, K_NO_WAIT);
		k_thread_join(&thread, K_FOREVER);
	}
	
	int main(void)
	{
		printk("Start\n");
		run_thread();
		printk("done\n"); // <-- crash
		k_sleep(K_FOREVER);
		return 0;
	}

kconfig:

	CONFIG_LOG=y

Build and run:

	west build -b qemu_cortex_a53 path/to/test -t run

review_comments: Why test both?  Surely the latter is the only one you need.
I agree, only the latter check is needed, and also that `arch_thread_end` is a better place for this eventually
